title: The Big Sister Who Taught India to Win: Harmanpreet Kaur's Captaincy Legacy
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down after 14 years as India women's captain, leaving behind the country's first senior ICC title and a winning culture that will outlast her.
body:
• Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as India women's captain this week, ending a leadership run that began in 2012 and peaked with the country's first senior ICC title.
  • Under her captaincy, India won the 2025 ODI World Cup — a 52-run victory over South Africa in Navi Mumbai — and she retired as the most successful captain in women's T20I history with 77 wins, surpassing Meg Lanning's 76.
  • Across 130 T20Is as skipper she scored 2,770 runs, the second-most by any captain in women's T20Is, and she reached 350 international appearances, a mark bettered only by New Zealand's Suzie Bates.
  • Smriti Mandhana has taken over as all-format captain. Harmanpreet, 36, stays on as a player ahead of the 2026 T20 World Cup in England and Wales.

Harmanpreet Kaur's captaincy of India ended the way few long reigns in sport do: with the job done. The BCCI on Tuesday named Smriti Mandhana as all-format captain, hours after Harmanpreet stepped down following India's Asian Games gold in Japan, closing a leadership era that stretched from a stand-in stint in 2012 to the 2025 ODI World Cup title — the first senior ICC trophy Indian women have ever lifted. She leaves having set the standards by which her successors will be judged.

Context and background

Leadership came to Harmanpreet by accident. On October 31, 2012, with Mithali Raj and Jhulan Goswami injured, she captained India in the Asia Cup final against Pakistan in Guangzhou and won it by 18 runs. In October 2016 she succeeded Mithali as full-time T20I captain, a role she held for nearly a decade.

https://x.com/CNBCTV18News/status/2107516699008454931

The early years were defined by near-misses. Her 171 not out off 115 balls against Australia in the 2017 ODI World Cup semi-final remains one of the great innings by an Indian; India lost the final to England. The T20 side reached the semi-finals in 2018 and 2023, lost the 2020 Melbourne final to Australia by 85 runs, and suffered a group-stage exit in 2024.

Then came 2025. In Navi Mumbai, India beat South Africa by 52 runs to win the ODI World Cup. Harmanpreet scored 260 runs in the tournament, including 89 off 88 balls in the semi-final, when she and Jemimah Rodrigues (unbeaten 127) chased down 339 against seven-time champions Australia. The image of the captain posing with the trophy in a t-shirt that read "Cricket is everyone's game" went around the world.

Impact and analysis

The numbers stack up as one of the great captaincy records in cricket. Her 77 T20I wins are the most in women's cricket history, one more than Meg Lanning's 76, and more than any man or woman has managed for India — Rohit Sharma won 49 of his 62 games as T20I captain. Across 130 T20Is as skipper she made 2,770 runs at a strike rate of nearly 115, the most by any women's T20I captain except Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu. In December 2025 she became only the second cricketer, after New Zealand's Suzie Bates, to play 350 internationals.

"I am very grateful and would like to give all the credit to my team."

— Harmanpreet Kaur, on becoming the most successful captain in women's T20I history

The deeper legacy is structural. Harmanpreet captained through the BCCI's pay-parity decision and the Women's Premier League's arrival, and she used her authority to back young players — Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma — until they became match-winners.

"Scoring 300-plus runs regularly in ODIs doesn't happen overnight. It's the result of consistent hard work and intent."

— Harmanpreet Kaur, on India's 2025 World Cup semi-final chase against Australia

Diaspora angle

Harmanpreet's arc — from a village outside Moga in Punjab, where she learned cricket with a hockey stick and played alongside boys, to the summit of the world game — has a particular resonance for diaspora families. After the World Cup win, coaches in Mumbai reported being flooded with calls from parents across age groups, and street celebrations erupted as far afield as Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh. For Indian parents abroad weighing weekend cricket academies for their daughters, the captain who just stepped down is the proof of concept.

What's next

Harmanpreet is not gone from the side. She remains in both squads for the home series against Zimbabwe — three T20Is in Raipur from October 16–20, then three ODIs in Vadodara from October 23–28 — and the 2026 T20 World Cup in England and Wales, starting June 12, is a realistic last dance. Mandhana, who overtook Mithali Raj in September as the leading run-scorer in women's internationals and holds the record of 18 international hundreds, inherits a team that expects to win. That expectation is Harmanpreet's doing. The big sister taught India to win; now she gets to watch her little sisters defend the habit.
